wins.text: Q4 revenue of $15.4B, up 10% YoY and $300M above guidance midpoint, beating expectations for the fourth consecutive quarter
CCG revenue of $8.8B, up 33% YoY with record notebook shipments; operating profit up ~$2.4B YoY
Q4 gross margin of 48.8%, 230 bps above guidance, driven by favorable product mix, ASPs and improved factory costs
IFS lifetime deal value more than doubled to over $10B from prior $4B update, with 4 Intel 18A foundry customers secured vs. 1 committed entering 2023
Delivered $3B cost savings commitment for FY2023 and achieved ~$2B net inventory reduction of 35 days from Q1 peak

risks.text: Q1 guidance of $12.2B–$13.2B (midpoint $12.7B) implies a sharp ~18% sequential revenue decline, with gross margin falling to ~44.5% and EPS of only $0.13

Material inventory corrections in Mobileye and PSG, plus IFS revenue drop from traditional packaging wind-down and cyclical wafer equipment weakness, creating ~$1B sequential headwind from non-core businesses
Data Center (DCAI) revenue expected to decline double-digit percent sequentially in Q1, with wallet share shifting from CPU to GPU accelerators
Depreciation expected to grow ~$2B in 2024 plus significant variable factory start-up costs, creating persistent headwinds on margin expansion pace
Telco/NEX markets expected to remain weak through the full year, with growth skewed to second half

guidance_items.detail: Q1 revenue guided to $12.2B–$13.2B (midpoint $12.7B), well below Q4's $15.4B; full-year expects sequential and YoY growth each quarter after soft Q1
Q1 gross margin guided to ~44.5%, down from Q4's 48.8%; 60% fall-through rule of thumb for full year with quarterly volatility expected
Q1 EPS guided to $0.13, down sharply from Q4's $0.54; full-year expects earnings to grow faster than revenue
Gross CapEx expected to increase in 2024 vs. 2023; net CapEx on track for mid-30s % of revenue aggregate 2023–2024
Roughly breakeven adjusted free cash flow maintained for full-year 2024; long-term 60% gross / 40% operating margin targets reaffirmed

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: GPU competitors capturing nearly all incremental cloud CapEx, leaving limited room for CPU revenue growth beyond seasonal variations
Persistent capacity utilization headwinds and timeline for internal wafer loading ramp (Panther Lake not in high volume until ~2026)
Competitive positioning of Intel 18A vs. TSMC given TSMC's continued investment in leadership nodes and Intel's ongoing use of external foundry for heterogeneous products
